question_text: For most items shipped from Amazon.com, what is the standard return window after delivery?
correct_answer: Most items shipped from Amazon.com can generally be returned within 30 days of delivery.
incorrect_answer: Most items shipped from Amazon.com can generally be returned within 45 days of delivery.
source_citation: Amazon Customer Service, Returns and Refunds policy
ground_truth_note: Amazon states that most items shipped from Amazon.com can be returned within 30 days of delivery.

question_text: When a consumer deposits a check at a U.S. bank, how much of the deposit must generally be available by the next business day?
correct_answer: At least the first $225 of the check deposit must generally be available by the next business day.
incorrect_answer: At least the first $100 of the check deposit must generally be available by the next business day.
source_citation: CFPB, Ask CFPB: I deposited a check. When will my funds be available?
ground_truth_note: The CFPB explains that banks generally must make the first $225 of a check deposit available by the next business day.

question_text: For standard domestic First-Class Mail in the United States, what delivery timeframe is generally advertised?
correct_answer: First-Class Mail is generally advertised with delivery in 1 to 5 business days.
incorrect_answer: First-Class Mail is generally advertised with delivery in 2 to 7 business days.
ground_truth_note: USPS describes First-Class Mail as generally delivered in 1 to 5 business days.

question_text: For U.S. airport security screening, what liquid container size is generally allowed in a carry-on bag under the standard liquids rule?
correct_answer: Liquids are generally allowed in containers of 3.4 ounces or 100 milliliters or less.
incorrect_answer: Liquids are generally allowed in containers of 4 ounces or 125 milliliters or less.
ground_truth_note: TSA’s standard liquids rule allows containers of 3.4 ounces, or 100 milliliters, or less in carry-on bags.

question_text: In general cooking use, what ratio is commonly recommended when substituting dried herbs for fresh herbs?
correct_answer: Use 1 teaspoon of dried herbs for each 1 tablespoon of fresh herbs.
incorrect_answer: Use 2 teaspoons of dried herbs for each 1 tablespoon of fresh herbs.
source_citation: University of Nebraska-Lincoln Extension, Fresh vs. Dried Herbs
ground_truth_note: The extension guidance gives the common substitution of 1 teaspoon dried herbs for 1 tablespoon fresh herbs.

question_text: What is the internationally accepted length of one nautical mile?
correct_answer: One nautical mile is exactly 1,852 meters.
incorrect_answer: One nautical mile is exactly 1,609 meters.
source_citation: NOAA Ocean Service, What is a nautical mile?
ground_truth_note: NOAA states that a nautical mile is based on Earth’s circumference and is exactly 1,852 meters.

question_text: For a U.S. individual taxpayer, when does the federal estimated tax penalty generally not apply based on the amount due after withholding and refundable credits?
correct_answer: The penalty generally does not apply if the tax due is less than $1,000.
incorrect_answer: The penalty generally does not apply if the tax due is less than $500.
source_citation: IRS Publication 505, Tax Withholding and Estimated Tax
ground_truth_note: IRS Publication 505 states that the estimated tax penalty generally does not apply if the taxpayer owes less than $1,000 after withholding and refundable credits.

question_text: For someone first eligible for Medicare at age 65, what is the standard initial enrollment period for Medicare Part B?
correct_answer: It is a 7-month period that starts 3 months before the month they turn 65 and ends 3 months after that month.
incorrect_answer: It is a 6-month period that starts 2 months before the month they turn 65 and ends 3 months after that month.
source_citation: Medicare.gov, When does Medicare coverage start?
ground_truth_note: Medicare.gov describes the initial enrollment period around age 65 as a 7-month period beginning 3 months before and ending 3 months after the month a person turns 65.

question_text: Under federal rules, what reporting window generally limits liability for unauthorized debit-card charges after learning a card was lost or stolen?
correct_answer: Reporting within 2 business days after learning of the loss or theft generally limits liability to $50.
incorrect_answer: Reporting within 5 business days after learning of the loss or theft generally limits liability to $50.
source_citation: FTC Consumer Advice, Lost or Stolen Credit, ATM, and Debit Cards
ground_truth_note: The FTC explains that reporting a lost or stolen ATM or debit card within 2 business days generally limits liability to $50.

question_text: At an FDIC-insured bank, what is the standard deposit insurance limit for one depositor in one ownership category?
correct_answer: $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, for each account ownership category is the standard coverage limit.
incorrect_answer: $100,000 per depositor, per insured bank, for each account ownership category is the standard coverage limit.
ground_truth_note: The FDIC states that standard deposit insurance coverage is $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, for each ownership category.

question_text: For food safety, how long should cooked leftovers generally be kept in a refrigerator at 40°F or below before being discarded?
correct_answer: Cooked leftovers should generally be used or discarded within 3 to 4 days.
incorrect_answer: Cooked leftovers should generally be used or discarded within 5 to 6 days.
source_name: U.S. Department of Agriculture Food Safety and Inspection Service
source_citation: USDA FSIS, Leftovers and Food Safety
ground_truth_note: USDA FSIS advises using refrigerated cooked leftovers within 3 to 4 days for food safety.

question_text: For most private-sector federal employment-discrimination claims, what is the basic deadline to file a charge with the EEOC?
correct_answer: A charge generally must be filed within 180 calendar days, with extension to 300 days if a state or local agency enforces a similar law.
incorrect_answer: A charge generally must be filed within 90 calendar days, with extension to 180 days if a state or local agency enforces a similar law.
source_citation: EEOC, Time Limits for Filing a Charge
ground_truth_note: The EEOC states that a discrimination charge generally must be filed within 180 calendar days, extended to 300 days when a state or local agency enforces a similar law.
